pages.title: Gut Health
pages.text:
Your gut flora is a separate hidden stat that tracks how well your digestive system is holding up.

It starts healthy and decays when you eat raw food. Let it get low enough and it starts amplifying the penalties you take — a bad gut makes raw food even worse.

pages.title: How It Decays
pages.text:
Every raw food event damages your gut flora by an amount based on the tier. $(#e05252)Severe$() foods do the most damage, $(#E8C24F)Mild$() foods do the least.

Gut damage doesn't happen instantly from one bad meal — it accumulates. Eating raw occasionally is survivable. Making it a habit is not.

pages.title: How It Recovers
pages.text:
Gut flora recovers passively over time as long as you aren't actively damaging it.

Eating $(#52c252)Dairy$() and $(#52c252)Vegetables$() speeds up recovery. These two food groups represent probiotic and fiber-rich foods that support a healthy gut — keep them topped up and you bounce back faster.

pages.title: Resistance
pages.text:
High Dairy and Vegetable nutrition also builds $(bold)resistance$() to raw food penalties.

A well-fed gut doesn't eliminate the penalties, but it reduces how hard each raw food event hits you. Keeping those two bars healthy is the closest thing to a buffer against the occasional raw meal.

pages.title: The Takeaway
pages.text:
Cook your food whenever possible. Keep Dairy and Vegetables topped up to maintain gut resistance and speed up recovery if you do take damage.

If your gut is already low, prioritize cooked meals and dairy until it recovers before worrying about the rest of your bars.
